label: Table
title: Table
summary: Use a Table to compare a few values across rows, such as holdings, with columns that line up and numbers aligned right.
corePrinciple: Line values up so they can be compared at a glance.

anatomy.title: A header row over rows of cells
anatomy.description: Each column has a grey header cell and a white cell in every row, with 1 px lines between them. Strings and numbers render as Coin Text; a column can render its own content instead.
blocks: Grey row of column names; it stays put when the rows scroll.
14 px semibold, aligned like the values below it.
One record, such as one holding; it can be pressable.
White, 12 px padding, with 1 px lines on its right and below.
Right-aligned, so digits line up down the column.

configuration.title: Columns, header, borders, and text modes
configuration.description: Columns share the width unless one gets a flex or a fixed width, and each sets its own alignment. The header and the outer lines can go. Modes on the table reach its body text only; text size and the brand appearances are in the playground above, and the header never changes.
blocks: Columns share the width equally; numbers sit right so their digits line up.
Asset takes twice the room and Units keeps a fixed 70 px; a fixed width beats flex.
Only the rows remain, for values that a title above already explains.
The last column and the last row drop their outer lines, for a table inside a card.
The Change column renders Coin Text, here green for gains and red for losses.
Success, Warning, and Error tint every body cell green, amber, or red; to mark one value, render your own cells.
Weight reaches the text cells: Bold makes every value bold. With no Weight they stay Regular.
Context retunes text sizes for where the table sits: under ListItem, Medium text is 12 px.
The values stay dark and readable on the white cells.

states.title: Static or pressable rows
states.description: Rows are static by default. When the screen handles a row press, every row takes focus and a press and fades while pressed; screen readers still hear it as a row. With no rows, only the header shows: the table has no empty message of its own.
blocks: Rows only show values; they can't be focused or pressed.
Each row takes focus and a press: it fades to 60% while pressed and tells the screen which holding it is.
Only the header shows. Put an Empty State next to it to explain why.

sizing.title: Fills its host, scrolls when it can’t fit
sizing.description: A table fills its host’s width. Cells have 12 px of padding and 1 px lines; rows are about 42 px tall at Medium text and the header about 45 px. Fixed widths that add up to more than the host need sideways scroll, or the last column is cut off. A maximum height scrolls the rows under a pinned header.
blocks: Columns keep 140, 90, 130, and 90 px; scroll sideways to reach Change. No scrollbar shows.
Ten holdings in 152 px: the rows scroll and the header stays put.
The header moves sideways with the rows but stays at the top.
In a 240 px host each column keeps about 30 px for text, so words and numbers break apart. Use fewer columns or sideways scroll.

sources.title: Use the public Table contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Table is one 720 × 190 component: a full-width header over a grid of white cells with 1 px grey lines. In code each column has its own header cell, a line runs under the header, and rows are a little taller; widths, alignment, and scrolling exist only in code. Developers can build the same table from data or from its parts. The app’s theme doesn’t reach the table, so it takes its modes directly, and they change body text only. Since the #264 fix, Weight reaches text cells, Page type JioPlus keeps them dark on white, and on the web screen readers hear the header cells, rows, and cells as a table, with pressable rows still rows. Biscuit’s main has the handwritten Storybook page.
